what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: Two of the four things I named last time are finished and can leave this file, and one of them is the best artefact the project has produced. The ceiling question came back reconciled rather than argued: the two figures that appeared to contradict each other -- "interior optima on 255 of 263" against "20 of 42 at the ceiling" -- were never in conflict, because `tools/couple_value_based_ pricing.py` passes `decide_margin` no `max_offered_rate_gbp_per_mwh` at all, so its `ceiling_bound` was a flag that could not fire and its near-zero count read exactly like a control that fired zero times. The reconciled answer is now in the artefact's own headline and it is not flattering: THE OPTIMUM IS INTERIOR TO WHAT THE COMPANY'S BELIEF SUPPORTS AND ABOVE WHAT THE COMPANY MAY LAWFULLY CHARGE. Priced with no cap the maximiser turns over inside its own support on 396 of 397 accounts; priced under the cap at a real term, half its answers sit on the cap. A margin pinned to a ceiling is a margin the arm did not choose, and the artefact says so where a reader will hit it. The divergence campaign also closed -- `background/tree_divergence.py` now reads 1 file at 0.87h against 436 six days ago, `severity()` and `ESCALATION_MULTIPLE` are landed with the mutation both ways, and the policy-cost tests are tracked. So the two items whose acceptance test was disappearance have disappeared. What did NOT happen is the one mechanical act at the top of the list. `python3 -m tools.run_value_cycle_ab` was never re-run. The book moved from the 131 accounts the A/B scored to 397 (395 resi, 2 SME, `site/data/company.json` 23:07:37Z), and the published answer -- net +GBP 16,773.28, EV +GBP 10,799.78 -- still describes 17:09:29Z. Worse, three instruments were BUILT for that reading and none of them has ever emitted a number: `gross_to_net_bridge` (the named decomposition of the GBP 30,924 gross-fell-while-net-rose gap, with `unexplained_residual_gbp` and a reconstruction error so a decomposition that does not close says so), `bound_attribution`, and `cross_section_reconciliation`. Grep every `value_cycle_ab*.json` on the tree and none of those keys exists. We spent the stretch sharpening the instrument and never took the reading. And the reading matters more than I thought, because the existing one contains something I had not looked at properly: the value arm repriced 42 renewals at a median GBP 57.75/MWh against the control's GBP 2.00 -- roughly a 28x commodity margin -- and the world answered with TWO extra churn events, 32 against 34 on a 131-account book. If the world barely punishes a 28x rise, then "the arm earns more" is a fact about the world's switching response, not about anything the arm inferred, and no amount of re-running fixes that. On the inference axis the news is unchanged and it is mine for the third time: EP1 was named in focus, drawn, and `saas/churn_model.py::churn_probability` is still `min(BASE_ANNUAL_CHURN_PROBABILITY + bill_shock_count * CHURN_UPLIFT_PER_BILL_SHOCK, MAX_CHURN_PROBABILITY)`. `coupled_gap_ledger.json` still reads `distinct_hazards: 1`, `hazard_histogram {"0.05": 33}`, a believed tenure of 20.0 years for every graded account, and it was measured at 11:46:22Z -- before the book changed twice. I ordered it second twice on the reasoning that the cheaper item gated it; the cheaper item consumed the stretch both times and did not produce the reading it was supposed to gate. That is my error, not the machine's, and it is corrected by putting EP1 first. Against the thesis: a supplier that decides customer-by-customer on LIFETIME VALUE, whose lifetime term takes exactly one value across every graded account, and whose measured advantage may be a fact about how forgivingly the world responds to price, has not yet shown the thing this project exists to show. The instrument is now good enough to find that out. It has not been pointed at the company.

focus.what: Give the tenure horizon per-account dispersion from observables the company can actually know. Third naming, first time first, and the diagnosis is settled -- do not re-derive it, and do not spend the tick re-reading the ledger. The subject is one function: `saas/churn_model.py::churn_probability` returns `min(BASE_ANNUAL_CHURN_PROBABILITY + bill_shock_count * CHURN_UPLIFT_PER_BILL_SHOCK, MAX_CHURN_PROBABILITY)`, a step function of one integer, consumed by `company/analytics/clv_three_horizon.py` at H2 as `hazard = latest.churn_probability` with the term `1.0 / hazard`. `coupled_gap_ledger.json` `components.lifetime_level` reads `distinct_hazards: 1`, `hazard_histogram {"0.05": 33}`, median believed tenure 20.0 years, measured 11:46:22Z. Note that `components.hazard_calibration` reports 13 distinct believed hazards over 263 decisions -- the estimator CAN take other values, and every one of the 33 graded accounts had zero bill shocks, which is why the graded population is a constant. So the defect is that the only input is an event most accounts never have. Widen the propensity to what a supplier observes about a household: payment method and payment behaviour, tenure to date, the account's own tariff against the market it could switch to, consumption volatility, contact and complaint history, and whether the account carries a gas leg -- 395 of the 397 accounts on the book are residential and the funnel now wins gas legs, so dual-fuel status is a live per-account observable rather than a hypothetical. Note the richer sibling before you write anything: `company/crm/churn_model.py::estimate_churn_probability` already takes tenure, bill stress, hedge fraction, segment and market move, so the shape you need may be a matter of reading the account's own signals through the wall rather than inventing a model. Check every input against the wall: if it needs a simulation internal it is a violation, and `company/interfaces/sim_interface.py` is the only door. The LEVEL is about right -- `hazard_calibration` shows 0.05 believed against 0.0532 realised over 263 decisions -- so this is DISPERSION, not calibration, and nothing may be tuned toward a smaller gap (R12). Re-measure with `python3 -m tools.couple_clv` and report the ledger's next reading whichever way it moves; a move to level 3 is available on this evidence if the coupled rung is genuinely met -- self-certify with `record_level_up_self_certified`, never `--no-verify` a `level_current` change.
focus.why: This is the sentence in the director's thesis stated as code. "Decisions customer-by-customer on lifetime value" and a lifetime term with one value across the whole graded population are the same claim and its refutation, sitting in one file. It is first because I have put it second twice, on the reasoning that a cheaper item gated it, and both times the cheaper item took the whole stretch and did not produce the reading it was supposed to gate -- a drawn item that leaves its named subject byte-identical twice running is drift, and this is the third naming. It is also first on merit rather than on penance: items two and three both report a number whose mechanism cannot be attributed while the belief behind it is a constant, and item three should be run ONCE, after the beliefs it scores have stopped moving. Finished when the graded population shows more than one distinct hazard, the ledger's next entry comes from a changed estimator rather than a changed sample, every new input is named with the observable it comes from and cleared against the wall, and the new gap is recorded whichever direction it went. If it worsens, that is the result and saying so is the deliverable.

focus.what: Measure what the world actually did when the arm raised prices, against what the company believed it would do, and report which side is wrong. The observation is already on the tree and needs no new run: `docs/observability/value_cycle_ab_resi.json` (17:09:29Z) has the value arm repricing 42 renewals at `median_margin_gbp_per_mwh` 57.75 against `control_margin_gbp_per_mwh` 2.00, and `churn_roster_diff` records 32 churn events under the control against 34 under the arm, on a book ending at 131 and 130 accounts. Take the arm's own renewal roster, recover the believed churn probability `company/crm/churn_model.py::estimate_churn_probability` produced for each of those 42 decisions at the price the arm actually chose, and compare the sum of those probabilities with the realised count of non-renewals among the same accounts. `RATE_SENSITIVITY` is 0.8 and `GAS_RATE_SENSITIVITY` 0.6 with a hedge reduction and a tenure discount, so the belief is not inert and the expected number is computable. Then say which of the three it is, with the arithmetic beside it: the company's belief over-predicts churn, or the world's switching response under-punishes a supplier-specific rise, or the sample of 42 is too small to separate them -- and if it is the third, say what would separate them. Read `belief_vs_outcome` (`discrimination_auc` 0.6944 on 24 matched decisions) beside it rather than instead of it: an arm can rank who leaves correctly while being wrong about how many. THE OUTPUT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A REPAIR. Changing the company's belief afterwards is the company's own affair and it is allowed to be wrong. Changing the WORLD's switching response is a fidelity change to the baseline, must be decided blind to what it does to this delta (R13), and is not this seat's; record it for the curriculum if that is where the arithmetic lands. Write it into `docs/design/THE_VALUE_CYCLE_REALISED_AB.md` as its own dated section.
focus.why: This decides whether the only number that answers the director's question means anything. The arm's advantage is supposed to come from INFERENCE and not from ACCESS, and the ceiling section landed this stretch establishes that it must not come from a BOUND either. There is a fourth way for it to be hollow that nothing has checked: it can come from a world that does not punish price. Forty-two renewals repriced at roughly 28x the control's commodity margin produced two extra churn events. If that is faithful, the arm's win is real but small and the lever is price rather than prediction; if it is the world being too forgiving, then every realised A/B result to date is a fact about the switching curve and the +GBP 16,773 headline cannot be attributed to inference no matter how many times it is re-run. This is the coupled triad on the pair that matters most -- company belief against world truth, gap reported -- and it is cheap, because both sides are already published. It is second rather than first only because item one changes a belief this measurement should be taken against once.

focus.why: The director asked for this directly and by name, it is the only item on this list he asked for in his own words, and I have held it out of focus twice on the grounds that the value cycle outranked it. Twice is the limit: a third deferral of a directly-asked item is how a request turns into a backlog entry. It also carries a live falsehood, which is the part that makes it focus rather than backlog -- an atom recorded at level 2 with no coupler and no ledger row is a level claim resting on evidence nothing has taken, and under the coupled triad no SIM atom reaches its target until the company has been tested against it and the gap measured. Fixing that changes a level or corrects one, which is what this list is for. It is fourth because the three items above are the one measurement the whole thesis rests on. Finished when either an EP13 row exists in `coupled_gap_ledger.json` with the company's carbon belief graded against the world's outturn, or the map entry says level 2 was unearned and now reads what the evidence supports.

what_next.why_this_is_here: Direction multiplies the draw's existing weights and can never zero one, so it can only ever be ignored -- never obeyed by force. Whether it was actually followed is therefore a measurement, not an assumption.

how_to_read_this: The delivery seat wakes on a timer, reads the last stretch, and writes direction -- never code. What it decides biases which work the ticks draw and can never block any of it. Everything on this page is read from a committed record; nothing here is computed a second time.
